**Tool:** kailash (release images) · **Section:** Getting started ·
**Level:** easy · **Time:** download 10–30 min · **Layer/Category:**
CLASSIC (image matrix) · **Tags:** getting-started, install, images,
verification

## Problem

You are starting from zero: you need a Kailash OS system to work in.
The deliverables are bootable images in two formats per profile (a
QEMU disk image — the primary shape — and a bootable ISO), published
as release assets on a signed tag. You want a downloaded artefact
you can state is exactly what the project built — checksums, build
provenance and the signed tag all agreeing — before anything boots.

## Solution

Pick your target from the declared matrix, download from the tagged
release, then run the three-step verification chain:

```bash
# 1. Download the artefact for your target from the tagged release
#    (e.g. the first release, 2026.01-alpha.1):
#      kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2
#    Above-cap artefacts ship split: <…>.part-000 (each chunk ≤1900 MiB)
#    plus a per-part sheet per chunk.

# 2. If chunked, reassemble — then run the whole-file check (the identity check):
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS-parts-kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2
cat kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2.part-* > \
    kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

# 3. Verify build provenance + the signed tag:
gh attestation verify kailash-2026.01-alpha.1-kailash-qemu-full.qcow2 \
    -R kailash-os/kailash-os
git tag -v 2026.01-alpha.1
```

What success looks like:

- the whole-file `sha256sum -c` against `SHA256SUMS` — the release
  sheet is THE authority on artefact identity — reports OK for your
  download
- `gh attestation verify` confirms SLSA v1.0 build provenance (plus
  the SPDX SBOM) built over the repo's OIDC identity, even after a
  chunk reassembly — the `cat` step is byte-exact, so the attested
  subject is preserved
- `git tag -v` shows a good GPG signature on the release tag
- the qcow2 boots in any UEFI-capable hypervisor (choose your own:
  QEMU/KVM, virt-manager, UTM on Apple Silicon); the ISO boots the
  same profile from optical/USB media

Every artefact is alternatively buildable from the release closure:

```bash
nix build github:kailash-os/kailash-os/2026.01-alpha.1#kailash-images-qemu-full
```

## Discussion

- **Which profile:** `minimal` boots the CORE substrate with no tool
  categories, `redteam-ai` is the AI red-team lab scope, `full` is
  the complete live catalogue, `headless-agent` is base + CLI with no
  desktop. The image name encodes the profile — see
  [First profile and first run](first-profile.html) for the
  profile table. Size budgets (≤1.5/4/8/10 GB by target) are enforced
  by construction; heavy corpora live in opt-in `kailash-data.*`
  packs, not in the default images — see
  [Refresh wordlists and data packs](data-packs.html).
- **Chunked assets are packaging, not fragility:** the 2 GiB legacy
  asset cap is answered with byte-exact split parts + per-part
  sheets on the same release; `cat` reproduces the original bits, and
  the attestation verifies the whole file after reassembly.
- **Aarch64 rows exist:** x86_64 targets are hosted-built; the
  aarch64 (Apple Silicon native) rows build via the project's
  `tools/build-arm-images.sh` — see the images chapter for the
  build-from-tag procedure.
- **Trust chain summary:** signed tag → SLSA provenance + SBOM per
  artefact → SHA256SUMS as the whole-file identity. A download that
  fails any link of that chain does not get booted — re-download or
  build from the tag yourself.
